target_customer: Field service and skilled trades companies (home services, HVAC and similar) that employ technicians; the company says it works with field operations firms in Florida, Pennsylvania and California
problem: Technicians document jobs poorly, which leaves the back office doing hours of manual work on dispatch, warranty claims and inventory.
business_model: B2B SaaS for field service companies (pricing not public)
product_category: AI operations layer for field service

founders.name: Luca Hadife
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built multimodal AI systems at Microsoft and was an early team member at Amata; also served as an ASUC Senator.

founders.name: Mohamed Hosny
founders.background_notes: YC page says he taught Computer Architecture and Signal Processing at UC Berkeley EECS and worked as a software engineer on data center switches at Arista. Degree not stated.

competitors.name: ServiceTitan Atlas
competitors.what: AI sidekick inside the ServiceTitan platform, with field-app answers for technicians and back-office automation
competitors.traction_then: Launched at Pantheon in September 2025 for ServiceTitan's existing contractor base; some features in private preview

competitors.name: Housecall Pro, Jobber, Zuper, ServiceMax, Salesforce Field Service
competitors.what: Field service software that all ship AI features such as CSR assistants, scheduling and Agentforce

technical_complexity.rationale: Capturing voice, photo and video from jobs into structured data and running agents over it is standard modern LLM engineering, with hard parts in accuracy and integrations with existing field service systems.

defensibility.rationale: Early product from a two person team; any moat would come from accumulated job data and integrations, while incumbents and rivals ship similar AI features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ServiceTitan launched Atlas in September 2025 and others added AI features; too early to know how it plays out.

market_need_then: Field service firms depend on technicians for documentation, and the company says poor documentation paralyzes the back office. Incumbent vendors were all adding AI in 2025 and 2026, which signals demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses kebra.com (exact .com); acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Simple Kebra wordmark in the navigation bar
identity.visual_style: Minimal landing page with large headline text
identity.voice_and_tone: Concise and confident, for example 'Technicians for the AI economy.'

brand_strength.rationale: New brand with no press about the brand itself; clean but unremarkable site and a name close to Tebra and other similar names.

outcome_analysis: Kebra is a Summer 2026 company with two founders from Microsoft and Arista backgrounds, so no outcome exists yet. A search for acquisition, shutdown or layoffs found nothing. The main risks visible today are incumbents such as ServiceTitan shipping Atlas in September 2025, and the need to prove accuracy across messy field data.
notes: Funding: Dealroom lists a $125k seed round with no investors named, seen only on one aggregator, so unverified and not recorded as a round. The company site says it is backed by Y Combinator, SV Angel and Browder Capital, but gives no amounts or dates. Outcome search returned nothing relevant.
